Program: Army Global Unified Network (AGUN) Increment 1
Organization: Leidos — Army & Mission Partners
Position Type: Full-Time, Dedicated Program Support
Location: Remote, with occasional travel as required-*Please be advised that during the interview, you will be required to keep your camera on, and your interviewer will be taking your picture for identification purposes, if an offer letter is extended to you.
Reports To: AGUN Program Management Office (PMO), with functional alignment to Leidos Subcontracts
Clearance: Active Secret Clearance and must maintain the clearance required by the program.


Position Summary

Leidos is seeking an experienced Subcontracts Manager to provide dedicated, on-program subcontract management support for the Army Global Unified Network (AGUN) Increment 1 program. AGUN is a large-scale Army network modernization effort supporting geographically dispersed installations, enterprise network operations, cybersecurity, engineering, and global deployment activities.

As AGUN expands into additional theaters and increases the concurrency of technical and operational requirements, the program requires dedicated subcontract management expertise to support resource planning, subcontract execution, financial controls, and supplier performance.

The selected candidate will work directly with the AGUN Program Manager, Deputy Program Manager, Finance, Contracts, and functional leads to ensure subcontract requirements are properly planned, authorized, funded, and executed.

Primary Responsibilities

  • Serve as the dedicated subcontract management representative embedded within the AGUN PMO.
  • Manage subcontract execution across multiple teaming partners supporting engineering, migration, installation, logistics, cybersecurity, and operations.
  • Coordinate subcontract modifications, funding actions, purchase orders, tasking, and contractual deliverables.
  • Support Technical Direction Letter (TDL) and Technical Direction Plan (TDP) development by validating subcontract labor, rates, staffing, scope, and execution requirements.
  • Monitor subcontract funding, ceiling limitations, labor utilization, commitments, and forecasted requirements.
  • Coordinate subcontract staffing plans, resource changes, mobilization, and demobilization across multiple geographic theaters.
  • Identify and resolve subcontract execution risks, including funding gaps, delayed authorizations, staffing availability, and supplier performance.
  • Support subcontractor proposal evaluations, cost/price analyses, negotiations, and documentation.
  • Ensure compliance with applicable prime contract requirements, subcontract terms, Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) requirements, and Leidos procurement policies.
  • Maintain accurate subcontract status reporting and provide timely recommendations to program leadership.
  • Coordinate closely with the program Financial Analyst to reconcile subcontract commitments, actual costs, and estimates to complete.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Business, Supply Chain Management, Finance, Contracts, or related discipline, with equivalent experience considered.
  • Typically 8–12 years of relevant subcontract management or federal contracting experience.
  • Experience supporting large Department of Defense or federal government programs.
  • Demonstrated knowledge of FAR/DFARS, subcontract administration, cost-reimbursement contracts, and Time & Materials subcontract structures.
  • Experience managing multiple subcontractors, funding actions, modifications, and supplier performance.
  • Strong financial, analytical, negotiation, and communication skills.
  • Ability to operate in a fast-paced program environment with competing priorities.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience supporting Army enterprise IT, network modernization, or large-scale systems integration programs.
  • Experience with CPFF/CPAF prime contracts and T&M subcontracts.
  • Familiarity with TDL/TDP execution models, BOEs, and integrated program financial management.
  • Experience supporting geographically distributed or overseas operations.
  • Familiarity with Leidos procurement and financial management systems.

Expected Outcomes

  • Improved subcontract funding and authorization visibility.
  • Faster coordination and execution of subcontract modifications.
  • Better alignment of subcontract staffing with approved work packages.
  • Reduced subcontract execution and compliance risk.
  • More accurate subcontract cost and resource forecasting.
  • Reduced administrative burden on the Program Manager and Deputy Program Manager.

If you're looking for comfort, keep scrolling. At Leidos, we outthink, outbuild, and outpace the status quo — because the mission demands it. We're not hiring followers. We're recruiting the ones who disrupt, provoke, and refuse to fail. Step 10 is ancient history. We're already at step 30 — and moving faster than anyone else dares.

Mit Deiner Arbeit bist Du eine wesentliche Stütze in unserer Projektrealisierung und hilfst dabei, den Qualitätsanspruch unserer Beratung sicherzustellen. Durch fundierte Analysen, Best-Practice-Ansätze und pragmatische Maßnahmen, die Du umsetzt, begeisterst Du unsere Kunden und förderst so unser Wachstum.

DAS BRINGST DU MIT

Wir sind auf der Suche nach motivierten und Start-up affinen Profilen mit den verschiedensten Backgrounds. Wir erwarten nicht, dass Du schon alle Skills perfekt kannst. Was Du noch nicht weißt, bringen wir Dir bei!
  • Du hast relevante Berufserfahrung im Bereich People & Culture, dabei auch dezidierte Berufserfahrung im Bereich People Operations / HR Systems
  • Ein abgeschlossenes wirtschaftswissenschaftliches Studium oder eine Ausbildung ist ein Plus
  • Du bist sehr gut in allen People Operations Prozessen (vom Onboarding bis zum Offboarding)
  • Du kennst Dich sehr gut mit verschiedensten HR-Tools (z.B. HRIS, ATS, L&D-, Feedback- oder Performance Management Systeme), der Implementierung und Administration dieser Tools und der Verbesserung und Automatisierung der Prozesse in den Tools aus
  • Du hast gute Kenntnisse der Prozess-Vereinfachung, -Digitalisierung und -Automatisierung im People-(Operations-)Bereich
  • Du hattest schon Berührungspunkte mit anderen HR-Aufgabengebieten (v.a. Business Partnering oder Performance Management)
  • Du hast gute Fähigkeiten in der Problemanalyse sowie der Aufbereitung, Visualisierung und Präsentation von Lösungsmöglichkeiten
  • Erste Erfahrungen in Projektmanagementaufgaben sind ein Plus
  • Erfahrungen mit Systeme wie HiBob, Personio, Leapsome, Tellent sind ein Plus
  • Du sprichst Deutsch auf muttersprachlichem Niveau und Englisch fließend (ca. B2)

DEINE ROLLE BEI UNS

  • Implementierung von Best-in-Class HR-Tools: z.B. HRIS, ATS, L&D-, Feedback- oder Performance Management Systeme, zusammen mit oder für unsere Kunden.
  • Unterstützung in und Übernahme von Beratungsprojektenzu Fragestellungen im Bereich HR Tooling sowie Prozessdigitalisierung und -Automatisierung für Start-ups, Scale-Ups und KMUs
  • Aufbau und Optimierungvon Prozessen sowie Digitalisierung und Automatisierung

  • Knowledge Sharing & Standards:Mitarbeit an unserer unternehmensinternen Wissensdatenbank zur kontinuierlichen Weiterentwicklung unserer Standards und Best Practices.

DAS ERWARTET DICH BEI UNS

  • Echte Flexibilität: Remote, Hybrid oder aus unseren Büros – du passt Arbeitsort und Arbeitszeiten an dein Leben an.
  • Maximale Lernkurve: Durch abwechslungsreiche Kundenmandate lernst du in kurzer Zeit unterschiedlichste HR-Setups, Unternehmenskulturen und Führungsmodelle kennen.
  • Interne Entwicklungspfade: Ob Fachexperte/Fachexpertin für Spezialthemen oder intern als People Lead – wir fördern deine persönliche und berufliche Entwicklung gezielt.
  • Starker Teamgeist: Kein Einzelkämpfertum – das gesamte Expert*innen-Team von Friday/Poppins hält dir als Sparringspartner den Rücken frei.

jobs.title: Director of PMO – Insurance & Investments
jobs.excerpt: Job Description: Director of PMO – Insurance & Investments 1.
jobs.description:
Job Description: Director of PMO – Insurance & Investments

1. Role Summary

The Director of Project Management Office (PMO) is responsible for establishing, leading, and managing the organization's Project Management Office to ensure effective governance, planning, execution, monitoring, and delivery of strategic and operational projects.

The role oversees the project portfolio across insurance, investment, corporate operations, technology, digital transformation, and business development functions. The Director of PMO ensures projects are delivered within approved timelines, budgets, quality standards, and organizational objectives while maintaining effective risk management, resource allocation, and stakeholder engagement.

The successful candidate will drive project management excellence, strengthen governance frameworks, improve delivery performance, and ensure that project outcomes contribute to business growth, operational efficiency, regulatory compliance, and customer experience.

2. Key Responsibilities

A. PMO Strategy, Leadership & Governance

  • Establish, develop, and lead the organization's Project Management Office.
  • Define PMO strategy, policies, methodologies, standards, and governance frameworks.
  • Implement standardized project management processes, tools, templates, and reporting structures.
  • Establish project approval processes, stage gates, escalation procedures, and accountability frameworks.
  • Promote project management best practices across departments and business units.
  • Ensure alignment between project execution and corporate strategy.

B. Project Portfolio Management

  • Oversee the organization's project portfolio, ensuring alignment with strategic priorities.
  • Evaluate project proposals, business cases, feasibility studies, and investment requirements.
  • Prioritize projects based on business value, financial impact, risk, and resource availability.
  • Monitor project dependencies, interdepartmental coordination, and portfolio-level risks.
  • Provide recommendations to senior management regarding project prioritization and resource allocation.
  • Track portfolio performance and ensure delivery of expected business benefits.

C. Project Planning & Execution

  • Oversee the planning, scheduling, budgeting, and execution of strategic projects.
  • Ensure project managers develop comprehensive project plans, milestones, deliverables, and resource requirements.
  • Monitor project progress and identify delays, delivery challenges, and performance gaps.
  • Drive corrective actions and escalation processes to maintain project delivery commitments.
  • Ensure projects are completed within approved scope, budget, timelines, and quality standards.
  • Coordinate cross-functional teams to ensure smooth project implementation.

D. Insurance & Investment Project Oversight

  • Oversee projects related to insurance operations, underwriting, claims management, policy administration, and distribution.
  • Coordinate initiatives involving investment operations, financial products, portfolio reporting, and client services, where applicable.
  • Support the implementation of regulatory, compliance, risk management, and internal control initiatives.
  • Monitor projects involving new product development, market expansion, operational improvements, and business integration.
  • Ensure project deliverables reflect the operational and regulatory requirements of the insurance and financial services industry.

E. Digital Transformation & Technology Projects

  • Oversee technology-enabled transformation projects, including core insurance systems, CRM, ERP, digital platforms, and automation initiatives.
  • Coordinate with IT, technology, operations, and business teams to ensure successful implementation.
  • Monitor technology project budgets, vendor performance, implementation timelines, and delivery quality.
  • Support digitalization, process automation, data management, and operational efficiency initiatives.
  • Ensure technology projects deliver measurable business outcomes.

F. Financial & Resource Management

  • Develop and monitor project budgets, financial forecasts, and expenditure reports.
  • Ensure effective allocation and utilization of project resources.
  • Monitor project costs, financial variances, and budget performance.
  • Evaluate project financial risks and recommend cost-control measures.
  • Coordinate with Finance and Procurement teams on project funding, contracts, and vendor payments.
  • Assess project return on investment (ROI) and benefits realization.

G. Risk Management, Compliance & Quality Assurance

  • Establish project risk management frameworks and escalation mechanisms.
  • Identify, assess, and monitor project risks, issues, dependencies, and delivery constraints.
  • Ensure projects comply with applicable regulatory requirements, internal policies, and governance standards.
  • Monitor project quality and ensure deliverables meet agreed specifications.
  • Maintain project documentation, audit trails, and management records.
  • Coordinate with Risk, Compliance, Legal, and Internal Audit teams.

H. Performance Monitoring & Executive Reporting

  • Develop project dashboards, management reports, and portfolio performance metrics.
  • Present project status, risks, budget performance, and delivery updates to executive leadership.
  • Provide timely visibility into project delays, resource constraints, and critical dependencies.
  • Monitor project KPIs and ensure accountability among project managers.
  • Lead project review meetings and portfolio governance sessions.
  • Recommend improvements to project delivery processes and organizational performance.

I. Stakeholder & Team Management

  • Lead and develop project managers, PMO analysts, and project support professionals.
  • Build strong working relationships with senior executives, department heads, project sponsors, and external vendors.
  • Facilitate communication and coordination across business units and functional teams.
  • Develop project management capabilities through training, coaching, and performance management.
  • Promote a culture of ownership, collaboration, transparency, and continuous improvement.

3. Required Qualifications & Experience

Educational Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Project Management, Finance, Engineering, Information Technology, or a related field.
  • Master's degree in Business Administration (MBA), Project Management, Finance, or a relevant discipline is preferred.

Professional Experience

  • Minimum 10–15 years of progressive professional experience in project management, program management, or portfolio management.
  • At least 5 years in a senior PMO leadership or Director-level position.
  • Proven experience establishing, managing, or transforming a Project Management Office.
  • Experience overseeing complex, enterprise-wide projects and cross-functional initiatives.
  • Background in insurance, banking, financial services, investment management, or related industries is highly desirable.
  • Experience managing large project portfolios, budgets, resources, and multiple project teams.
  • Exposure to digital transformation, technology implementation, business process improvement, and organizational change initiatives.

Preferred Certifications

- Project Management Professional (PMP).

- PRINCE2 Practitioner.

- Managing Successful Programmes (MSP).

  • Portfolio Management Professional (PfMP).

- Agile or Scrum certifications.

- Lean Six Sigma certification.

Core Competencies

  • Strategic project and portfolio management.
  • PMO governance and operational leadership.
  • Financial planning and budget management.

- Risk assessment and problem-solving.

  • Executive communication and stakeholder management.
  • Change management and business transformation.
  • Leadership, team development, and decision-making.
  • Project management systems and reporting tools.

4. Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

  • Percentage of projects delivered on time and within approved budgets.
  • Overall project portfolio performance and delivery success rate.

- Project cost and schedule variance.

  • Achievement of project milestones and strategic objectives.

- Project benefits realization and ROI.

  • Effectiveness of project governance and reporting.
  • Project risk identification, mitigation, and resolution.
  • Resource utilization and allocation efficiency.
  • Stakeholder satisfaction and project sponsor feedback.
  • PMO process maturity and continuous improvement.
  • Compliance with project management standards and regulatory requirements.

jobs.title: Chief Program Officer (CPO) – Insurance & Investments
jobs.description:
Chief Program Officer (CPO) – Insurance & Investments

1. Role Summary

The Chief Program Officer (CPO) is responsible for overseeing the organization's strategic programs, enterprise-wide initiatives, and complex, multi-project portfolios across its insurance and investment businesses.

The role ensures that major programs are strategically aligned, properly resourced, effectively governed, and successfully delivered within approved timelines and budgets. The CPO will establish program management standards, coordinate cross-functional teams, manage interdependent projects, and ensure that strategic initiatives deliver measurable business outcomes.

Working closely with the CEO, Board, and executive leadership team, the CPO will translate corporate priorities into coordinated programs that support business growth, operational excellence, digital transformation, regulatory compliance, and organizational development.

2. Key Responsibilities

Strategic Program Management

  • Develop and implement the organization's enterprise-wide program management strategy.
  • Identify, structure, prioritize, and oversee strategic programs aligned with corporate objectives.
  • Translate organizational strategies into coordinated programs with clear goals, milestones, deliverables, and expected outcomes.
  • Manage interdependencies between projects, business units, and strategic initiatives.
  • Monitor program performance and ensure alignment with organizational priorities.

Insurance & Investment Program Delivery

  • Lead strategic programs involving life insurance, general insurance, reinsurance, investment management, wealth management, and financial services.
  • Oversee programs related to insurance product development, underwriting modernization, claims transformation, policy administration, and distribution expansion.
  • Coordinate investment-related programs involving portfolio management systems, investment operations, client reporting, and service delivery, where applicable.
  • Manage initiatives involving regulatory changes, new business models, market expansion, and operational restructuring.
  • Ensure program deliverables address business requirements and relevant industry regulations.

Program Governance & Management Office

  • Establish and oversee program governance frameworks, methodologies, policies, and reporting standards.
  • Develop program charters, business cases, implementation plans, risk registers, and performance dashboards.
  • Implement structured review processes, approval mechanisms, escalation procedures, and executive reporting.
  • Ensure consistency in program management practices across subsidiaries and business units.
  • Work with the Project Management Office (PMO) to coordinate individual project delivery and maintain portfolio visibility.

Program Budget & Resource Management

  • Develop and oversee program budgets, resource plans, and financial forecasts.
  • Monitor program expenditure, financial performance, and budget variations.
  • Ensure effective allocation of people, technology, and financial resources across programs.
  • Evaluate program business cases, cost-benefit analysis, expected returns, and benefits realization.
  • Manage external consultants, contractors, technology vendors, and implementation partners.

Digital & Business Transformation Programs

  • Lead cross-functional programs involving digital transformation, automation, AI, cloud adoption, and enterprise system modernization.
  • Coordinate implementation of digital insurance platforms, customer portals, CRM systems, and investment service technologies.
  • Work with CIO, CTO, CDO, and business leaders to ensure technology programs deliver business value.
  • Oversee business process redesign, operational improvement, and organizational change initiatives.
  • Monitor adoption, implementation effectiveness, and long-term program outcomes.

Risk, Compliance & Quality Management

  • Identify, assess, and manage program-level operational, financial, regulatory, and technology risks.
  • Ensure programs comply with applicable insurance, investment, financial services, and corporate governance requirements.
  • Coordinate with risk, compliance, legal, and internal audit teams.
  • Establish mitigation strategies, contingency plans, and escalation mechanisms.
  • Monitor program quality and ensure deliverables meet approved standards.

Stakeholder & Executive Management

  • Collaborate with the CEO, Board, executive leadership, and business unit heads to define program priorities.
  • Coordinate communication and collaboration among project sponsors, program managers, and key stakeholders.
  • Manage relationships with regulators, external consultants, strategic partners, and implementation vendors, as appropriate.
  • Resolve conflicts involving program scope, resource allocation, timelines, and competing business priorities.
  • Present program progress, financial performance, key risks, and strategic recommendations to senior management.

Leadership & Program Management Excellence

  • Lead and develop program directors, program managers, project managers, and program delivery teams.
  • Build a high-performing program management function with clear accountability and performance standards.
  • Establish training, mentoring, and professional development initiatives.
  • Promote consistent program management methodologies and continuous improvement.
  • Introduce tools and reporting systems to improve program visibility, coordination, and delivery effectiveness.

3. Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Finance, Project Management, Engineering, Information Technology, or a related field.
  • MBA or Master's degree in Program Management, Business Strategy, Finance, or a relevant discipline preferred.
  • 12–15+ years of progressive experience in program management, project portfolio management, enterprise transformation, or strategic initiative delivery.
  • At least 5 years in a senior leadership role overseeing large-scale, multi-project programs.
  • Experience in insurance, reinsurance, banking, investment management, asset management, wealth management, or financial services preferred.
  • Proven track record of successfully delivering complex, cross-functional programs with measurable business outcomes.
  • Strong knowledge of program governance, project management methodologies, budgeting, risk management, and resource planning.
  • Experience establishing or leading enterprise program management offices.
  • Familiarity with Agile, Waterfall, PRINCE2, PMI, and hybrid delivery methodologies.
  • Excellent leadership, strategic planning, communication, stakeholder management, and problem-solving capabilities.

Preferred Certifications:

  • Program Management Professional (PgMP).

- Project Management Professional (PMP).

  • Portfolio Management Professional (PfMP).

- PRINCE2 Practitioner.

- Agile or Scrum certifications.

4. Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

  • Percentage of strategic programs delivered on time and within budget.
  • Program performance against approved strategic objectives.
  • Achievement of program milestones and deliverables.
  • Program budget variance and resource utilization.
  • Benefits realization and return on investment (ROI).
  • Effective management of project interdependencies.
  • Program risk mitigation and issue resolution effectiveness.
  • Stakeholder satisfaction and executive reporting quality.
  • Compliance with program governance and reporting standards.
  • Successful delivery of digital, operational, and business transformation programs.
  • Reduction in program delays, cost overruns, and implementation risks.

jobs.title: Director, Clinical Research
jobs.excerpt: About Hello Heart:Hello Heart is on a mission to make heart attacks a thing of the past.
jobs.description:
About Hello Heart:

Hello Heart is on a mission to make heart attacks a thing of the past.

We’re an AI company focused exclusively on heart health, building a platform that predicts and prevents cardiac events before they happen—identifying risk up to 10 days in advance versus 10 years in traditional clinical models.

This is already working at scale. Hello Heart has been shown to reduce inpatient hospital days by 47% and deliver ~$1,800 in annual savings per member. Hello Heart is the cardiac prevention partner to over 80% of large U.S. health plans and serves hundreds of public and private employers.

We’re defining how the #1 cause of death—heart disease—is managed in the AI era. Join us.

About the Role

Hello Heart is seeking a Director, Clinical Research to lead the clinical and economic evidence strategy to showcase how Hello Heart products help members understand and improve their heart health through AI, hardware, and behavioral science.

Reporting into our VP, Commercial Actuary, you will set our research and publications strategy; partnering with Commercial & Product Leadership, Medical Affairs, Data Science, Product, Sales, and Marketing to drive peer reviewed publications, white papers, conference abstracts, and client facing evidence that support our commercial goals. You will apply your expertise in statistics, claims analysis, and clinical research to shape our study pipeline, build partnerships with leading research institutes and consultants, and represent Hello Heart’s evidence to technical and executive audiences.

This is a strong fit for someone who enjoys rigorous research, clear communication, cross-functional collaboration, and turning complex data into evidence that supports better heart health outcomes.

What you’ll do

  • Collaborate with leadership and cross-functional partners to prioritize clinical and economic research priorities.
  • Provide peer review and mentorship to other researchers on the team, developing their analytical and publication skills over time.
  • Generate research questions and develop analytical plans for key publication and evidence-generation priorities.
  • Develop partnerships and work alongside leading research institutes.
  • Build Hello Heart's research and evidence strategy to support future FDA-regulated capabilities, accounting for regulatory requirements and timelines.
  • Identify, organize, query, and analyze diverse datasets, including clinical, claims, electronic health record (EHR), and engagement data.
  • Apply advanced statistical methods, including multilevel modeling, causal inference methods, propensity score matching, mixed-effects modeling, longitudinal analyses, and sensitivity testing.
  • Collaborate with co-authors to incorporate feedback and finalize analyses, manuscripts, white papers, and abstracts.
  • Respond to anonymous peer reviews, including repeat analyses and manuscript revisions, to support timely resubmission.
  • Identify relevant conferences for abstract submission and present ongoing research when appropriate.
  • Stay current on scientific research related to cardiovascular health, digital health, behavioral science, chronic disease, health economics, and public health.
  • Contribute to data summaries, research protocols, institutional review board (IRB) materials, and other research documentation.
  • Translate complex analytical findings into clear, accurate, and actionable insights for clinical, technical, commercial, and executive audiences.

What you’ll bring

  • Graduate degree in a clinical field, epidemiology, biostatistics, public health, or a related field, such as Master of Science (MS), Master of Public Health (MPH), Doctor of Philosophy (PhD), or Doctor of Pharmacy (PharmD), with 10+ years of clinical research experience.
  • Demonstrated experience working in a commercial research setting, comfortable balancing scientific rigor with business needs.
  • Experience leading or mentoring a team of researchers, including peer-reviewing others' work and supporting less experienced researchers as they develop toward independent publication.
  • Strong statistical programming experience with R, Python, SQL, MS Excel, or other relevant analytical tools.
  • Strong AI fluency, with the ability to design AI-enabled workflows, such as building or customizing agents others can use while maintaining accuracy, privacy, and human review.
  • Strong data skills, including data cleaning, data management, statistical analysis, and data visualization.
  • Experience planning and implementing complex statistical analyses while managing deadlines across multiple research priorities.
  • Experience working with clinical, claims, electronic health record (EHR), engagement, or other healthcare datasets.
  • Experience testing medical claims, pharmacy claims, and enrollment data for errors, including actuarial summaries and cuts by cohort.
  • Highly organized, detail-oriented, and able to manage multiple projects at once.
  • Open and responsive to feedback on manuscripts, analyses, and other written work.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain findings to technical and non-technical audiences.

The US base salary range for this full-time position is $180,000.00 to $197,000.00. Salary ranges are determined by role and level. Compensation is determined by additional factors, including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training. Please note that the compensation details listed in US role postings reflect the annual salary only, and do not include equity or benefits.

Hello Heart has a positive, diverse, and supportive culture - we look for people who are collaborative, creative, and courageous. Oh, and if you want to see some recent evidence of the fun things we do at Hello Heart, check out our Instagram page.
